extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU (Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning) is a benchmark of 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering) across 30 subjects and 183 subfields, featuring 30 heterogeneous image types and interleaved text-image inputs.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: University students and co-authors specializing in various majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials. New questions were created based on annotators' expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations and to select questions without immediately available answers to avoid data contamination.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials across 30 subjects from six disciplines, resulting in a diverse collection of 13K questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students specializing in relevant majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise. Annotators were instructed to follow copyright/license regulations and to select questions without immediately available answers. Data quality control involved duplicate detection, format/typo checking by co-authors, and difficulty categorization into four levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), with ~10% excluded for being too simple.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicates, which were then reviewed by authors. Co-authors performed format and typo checking. Difficulty levels were assigned and ~10% of problems classified as very easy were excluded. Error analysis was conducted on 150 annotated GPT-4V errors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. Additionally, GPT-4V often exhibits a bias in perceptual tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The benchmark combines multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions, which may limit assessment of fully open-ended responses.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU aims to evaluate capabilities of Large Multimodal Models toward Expert AGI, with strong performance on this benchmark considered a necessary criterion for an Expert AGI system.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) across professional domains, assessing both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities at the college level.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data quality control involved two steps: (1) lexical overlap and source URL similarity checks to identify and eliminate duplicate problems, followed by author review; (2) format and typo checking by co-authors to ensure standardized formatting. Additionally, approximately 10% of problems classified as 'very easy' were excluded from the benchmark.

name.evidence: We introduce MMMU: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.

description.evidence: MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types
